text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
KOHA JONE
- The editorial says the United States convinced Europe that a poor Albania but with a degraded regime would only bring about problems.
- The daily quotes the British newspaper Daily Telegraph saying Albanian dirty money from smuggling organised by a ruling Democratic Party company have been deposited in banks in England.
- Journalist of the British daily Independent Andrew Gumble repeats his allegations in an interview to BBC for the ruling party officials organising an illegal business.
- Police and rain did not allow Albanian protestors hold a rally last Sunday.
- A newspaper commentary says if the Albanian right-wing does not move it will turn into a utopia their idea of taking power in the post-communist country.
- The right-wing democratic Party blames uncontrolled state segments for the beating of its journalist Genc Cobani last weekend.
- Price increase of electricity, water supply and telephone service is expected while the government has still not passed the annual state budget.
- Trial against the last communist President Ramiz Alia, charged of genocide and crimes against humanity, starts on Tuesday.
- Seven people died and two are still in a grave situation at a tragic road accident in the northern village of Ternove e Madhe, Bulqize district.
- Protests against the collapse of the pyramid schemes were held in the last days in Vlore, Fier and other southern towns.

- Albania's government with a letter sent to the soccer federation by state sports secretary Marjeta Zace ordered the re-start of the national soccer championship after league was suspended for one month because of unrest sparked by the collapse of five pyramid investment schemes.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Political parties in southern Vlore said they would start a hunger strike if Aleksander Meksi government, blamed for the collapse of the pyramid schemes, did not resign.

- Political parties have already started a struggle of 'invitations for talks' with the leadership of the opposition Socialist Party still debating on the invitation by the ruling Democratic Party for bilateral talks on the current crisis on Wednesday while the opposition grouping of some political parties Forum for Democracy called for a roundtable.
- The right-wing National Front asked for the government resignation and the extension of President Sali Berisha's mandate until the current crisis is resolved.
- Italian press reports a still unconfirmed news that World Bank might give a credit of $50-100 million to Albania to resolve the pyramid investment scheme crisis.
- The European Union will debate on Febnruary 24 on Albania's case.
- Italy intensificates the control of the Adriatic Sea fearing an exodus from the Albanians suffering from the pyramnid scheme failure.
